issues.description: The UML in the problem statement indicates the Lecture attributes are private ( '-' visibility ), and the solution defines all attributes as private. However, the template Lecture.java exposes two attributes as public (lectureName and numberOfInscribedStudents). This visibility mismatch can confuse students about whether to access fields directly or via getters/setters and conflicts with the UML and solution, which expect private fields and corresponding accessor methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's public attributes to private to match the UML and solution (e.g., make lectureName and numberOfInscribedStudents private) and add the remaining private attributes as specified. Keep method stubs (getters/setters) in the template so students implement the expected accessors rather than accessing fields directly.
